items.readable_text:
Content:
Why do the exterior angles of a polygon always sum to [MATH: 360^\circ?]

Content:
Suppose we have an [MATH: n]-sided polygon. Then, we have the following:

Content:
- There are [MATH: n] pairs of interior-exterior angles, each pair being supplementary (i.e., their measures add to [MATH: 180^\circ).]
- Therefore, the sum of the measures of all interior-exterior pairs equals [MATH: {\color{blue}n\cdot 180^\circ}.]
- In a previous lesson, we saw that the sum of the interior angles equals [MATH: {\color{red}{(n-2)\cdot 180^\circ}}.]

Content:
Therefore, to get the sum of the exterior angles, we subtract [MATH: {\color{red}{(n-2)\cdot 180^\circ}}] from [MATH: {\color{blue}n\cdot 180^\circ}] as follows:
[MATH: Sum of Exterior Angles|= n ⋅ 180^{∘} − (n − 2) ⋅ 180^{∘}; = n ⋅ 180^{∘} − n ⋅ 180^{∘} + 2 ⋅ 180^{∘}; = n ⋅ 180^{∘} − n ⋅ 180^{∘} + 2 ⋅ 180^{∘}; = 2 ⋅ 180^{∘}; = 360^{∘}]

Content:
This proves that the sum of the exterior angles of a (simple) polygon equals [MATH: 360^\circ.]

Item 14 — Tutorial: Proving the Theorem

Content:
Why do the exterior angles of a polygon always sum to [MATH: 360^\circ?]

Content:
Suppose we have an [MATH: n]-sided polygon. Then, we have the following:

Content:
- There are [MATH: n] pairs of interior-exterior angles, each pair being supplementary (i.e., their measures add to [MATH: 180^\circ).]
- Therefore, the sum of the measures of all interior-exterior pairs equals [MATH: {\color{blue}n\cdot 180^\circ}.]
- In a previous lesson, we saw that the sum of the interior angles equals [MATH: {\color{red}{(n-2)\cdot 180^\circ}}.]

Content:
Therefore, to get the sum of the exterior angles, we subtract [MATH: {\color{red}{(n-2)\cdot 180^\circ}}] from [MATH: {\color{blue}n\cdot 180^\circ}] as follows:
[MATH: Sum of Exterior Angles|= n ⋅ 180^{∘} − (n − 2) ⋅ 180^{∘}; = n ⋅ 180^{∘} − n ⋅ 180^{∘} + 2 ⋅ 180^{∘}; = n ⋅ 180^{∘} − n ⋅ 180^{∘} + 2 ⋅ 180^{∘}; = 2 ⋅ 180^{∘}; = 360^{∘}]

Content:
This proves that the sum of the exterior angles of a (simple) polygon equals [MATH: 360^\circ.]
